name: DRV8434PWPR
title: DRV8434: 48 V, 2.5 A full-scale stepper driver with on-chip current sensing, STEP/DIR indexer to 1/256 microstep and smart tune decay
summary: A bipolar stepper motor driver with two N-channel H-bridges (330 mΩ high side plus low side at 24 V, 25 °C), an indexer driven by STEP and DIR from full step to 1/256 microstep, and current sensing done inside the chip so no sense resistors are fitted. It runs from 4.5 V to 48 V and drives up to 2.5 A full-scale or 1.8 A rms, set by the VREF voltage; decay is selectable among smart tune, slow and mixed modes. Protection covers VM and charge-pump undervoltage, overcurrent, open load and overtemperature, reported on nFAULT. DRV8434PWPR is the 28-pin HTSSOP PowerPAD part; DRV8434RGER is the 24-pin 4 mm VQFN.

circuits.title: Figure 8-1. Typical application, HTSSOP-28 (PWP) (1/8 microstepping, smart tune Ripple Control decay)
circuits.description: One bipolar stepper motor on the two bridges, run from a 24 V VM rail by STEP and DIR from a controller, which also drives nSLEEP and ENABLE. M0 and M1 are both tied to DVDD (1/8 step); DECAY1 to DVDD with DECAY0 grounded selects smart tune Ripple Control, and TOFF grounded gives the smallest ripple setting (19 mA + 1% of ITRIP). RREF1 and RREF2 divide VCC down to VREF, which sets the full-scale current. The charge pump uses 0.022 µF between CPH and CPL and 0.22 µF from VCP to VM. Each VM pin has 0.01 µF, with 100 µF bulk; DVDD has 0.47 µF and also pulls nFAULT up through 10 kΩ. The thermal pad connects to system ground.

operation.text: Two N-channel MOSFET H-bridges, a microstepping indexer and current sensing by a current mirror on the power MOSFETs (no sense resistors) in one chip for a bipolar stepper. Supply range 4.5 V to 48 V; output current ratings are 4 A peak, 2.5 A full-scale and 1.8 A rms, the usable full-scale and rms values depending on ambient temperature, supply voltage and the board's thermal design. Pin-compatible with DRV8426, DRV8436 and DRV8424/25. Both the digital oscillator and the charge pump use spread-spectrum clocking to reduce radiated emissions.

Peak current is set by the overcurrent trip IOCP, whose minimum gives a peak rating of 4 A per bridge, applying to short pulses at low duty. The rms rating, 1.8 A per bridge, comes from thermal limits (RDS(ON), edge times, PWM frequency, quiescent current, package) for a typical board at 25 °C and moves up or down with heatsinking and ambient. Full-scale current is the top of the sine the indexer produces.

M0 and M1 select full step (100% or 71% current), non-circular half step, half step, or 1/4 to 1/256 microstepping, and can be changed while running; the indexer then moves to the next valid state of the new mode at the next STEP rising edge. After power-up, leaving UVLO or leaving sleep, the indexer starts at 45° electrical, 71% of full scale in both windings. Full step at 100% and non-circular half step draw more power than their circular counterparts and give more torque at high speed.

VREF can come from a divider (from DVDD or another supply), a DAC, or a filtered PWM signal; a higher VREF gives a higher full-scale current. VREF must not exceed 3.3 V. For a divider the parallel value of the two resistors stays under 50 kΩ.

Fixed off-time PWM: with the bridge driving, winding current rises at a rate set by supply voltage, inductance and back-EMF until it reaches the trip level, then the bridge decays for the off-time set by TOFF and drives again. A comparator watches the voltage on sense MOSFETs paralleled with the low-side FETs, biased by a sine-shaped current DAC; VREF scales that DAC's full-scale value. After each turn-on the comparator is blanked for about 1 µs (tBLANK), which is also the minimum drive time.

DECAY0 and DECAY1 select smart tune Dynamic Decay, smart tune Ripple Control, mixed decay (30% or 60% fast), slow decay, or slow on rising steps with 30% mixed on falling steps. Changes take effect after a 10 µs deglitch. Fast decay reverses the bridge; slow decay turns on both low-side FETs. In full step and non-circular half step the falling-step decay mode is always used. Slow decay gives the least ripple but follows falling steps slowly and can lose regulation when back-EMF is small (motor held or stepping very slowly); mixed decay, fast for the first part of tOFF and slow for the rest, keeps regulation in that case at the cost of more ripple.

Picks slow, mixed or fast decay on every PWM cycle and adjusts the fast share of mixed decay: overshoot of the trip level makes the next cycle more aggressive, a long drive time makes it less so. On falling steps it switches to fast decay. It keeps a fixed off-time, so PWM frequency stays fixed, and adapts to winding resistance and inductance, ageing, speed and load, supply changes and back-EMF.

Adds a valley level IVALLEY under ITRIP: on reaching ITRIP the bridge goes into slow decay until the current falls to IVALLEY, so the off-time varies with conditions. The ripple, set by TOFF, is 19 mA plus 1%, 2%, 4% or 6% of the present ITRIP. Small ripple settings keep the PWM frequency out of the audible range; larger ripple lowers PWM frequency and switching loss.
Generates the high-side gate-drive supply, about VM + 5 V, at 360 kHz. It needs a storage capacitor from VCP to VM and a ceramic flying capacitor between CPH and CPL.

Internal linear regulator, nominally 5 V, for logic; it can source up to 2 mA and its voltage drops sharply above that. It may supply VREF through a divider and the nFAULT pull-up. Inputs that must be permanently high (Mx, DECAYx, TOFF) are best tied to DVDD: when VM is off or the part sleeps, DVDD shuts down and no current flows in the input pulldowns (typically 200 kΩ). Tying nSLEEP to DVDD would keep the device asleep for good.

STEP, DIR and nSLEEP are two-level logic inputs. M0, DECAY0 and ENABLE are tri-level (low, Hi-Z, high); DECAY1 has its own input structure. M1 and TOFF are quad-level: low, 330 kΩ to GND, Hi-Z, high. Logic inputs accept 1.8 V, 3.3 V and 5 V levels.
Open-drain output, pulled up to 5 V, 3.3 V or 1.8 V; low during a fault and high after power-up. A 5 V pull-up may go to DVDD through a resistor; 3.3 V or 1.8 V needs an external supply.

If VM falls below VUVLO, all outputs and the charge pump turn off and nFAULT goes low; operation resumes when VM recovers. If VCP falls below VCPUV, outputs turn off and nFAULT goes low while the charge pump keeps running; operation resumes when VCP recovers.

Each MOSFET has an analog current limit that removes its gate drive. If the limit lasts longer than tOCP, both bridges turn off and nFAULT goes low; the charge pump keeps running. ENABLE at Hi-Z gives latched shutdown, which an nSLEEP reset pulse or power cycling clears once the fault is gone; ENABLE high (above 2.7 V) gives automatic retry after tRETRY. The mode can be changed while running.

An open load is flagged when the current in a winding stays below both IOL and the indexer's ITRIP for longer than tOL; it is report only. With ENABLE tied to DVDD, nFAULT releases as soon as the condition clears; with ENABLE at Hi-Z it releases after the condition clears and an nSLEEP reset pulse. A power cycle or leaving sleep also clears it.

Above TOTSD all bridge MOSFETs and the charge pump turn off and nFAULT goes low. ENABLE at Hi-Z latches: recovery needs the die below TOTSD - THYS_OTSD and then an nSLEEP reset pulse or power cycle. ENABLE high retries automatically once the die is below TOTSD - THYS_OTSD.

nSLEEP low puts the device to sleep after tSLEEP: bridges, charge pump, DVDD regulator and logic off. Bringing nSLEEP high wakes it; inputs are accepted after tWAKE. With nSLEEP high, ENABLE low holds the outputs at Hi-Z while the rest keeps running; ENABLE high or Hi-Z with VM above UVLO is the operating mode.

A low pulse on nSLEEP longer than 20 µs and shorter than 40 µs clears latched faults without disturbing the charge pump or other blocks. A low between 40 µs and 120 µs clears faults and may or may not put the device to sleep.
STEP high and low times are at least 970 ns each; DIR and the mode pins need 200 ns setup and hold around the STEP rising edge. STEP may run up to 500 kHz.

VM runs from 4.5 V to 48 V. Each VM pin needs a 0.01 µF ceramic rated for VM placed as close as possible, plus bulk capacitance on VM. How much bulk is needed depends on peak motor current, the supply's own capacitance and current capability, wiring inductance between supply and driver, allowed ripple, motor type and braking method; it is settled by system testing. The bulk capacitor's voltage rating sits above the operating voltage to absorb energy the motor returns to the supply.

Bypass VM to PGND with a low-ESR 0.01 µF ceramic rated for VM, right at the VM pin, joined to PGND by a wide trace or ground plane; add VM-rated bulk capacitance, which may be electrolytic. Put a low-ESR 0.022 µF ceramic rated for VM between CPL and CPH and a low-ESR 0.22 µF 16 V ceramic between VM and VCP, both as close to their pins as possible. DVDD gets a low-ESR 0.47 µF 6.3 V ceramic to ground near its pin. The thermal pad connects to system ground.
